To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a set of robust X-band and 2-18GHz band GaN MMICs have been developed, and that they demonstrate state-of-the art survivability to CW power levels.

(i) a GaN process with high robustness to CW power is presented; (ii) a set of robust MMIC T/R components is presented and (iii) the development of high power amplifiers, robust LNAs and T/R switches in GaN will bring to the development of fully-integrated front-ends.
the GaN MMICs developed in this project have been successfully tested and demonstrated their robustness to CW input power level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of GaN monolithic MMICs for the integration of T/R module front-ends.
the development of a set of robust MMICs for T/R module front end integration.
the development of high power, low noise and robust GaN MMICS for future T/R module integration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of GaN MMICs for the front-end of T/R modules is possible and that the robustness of GaN MMICS has been demonstrated.
the development of the GaN MMIC chipset is a key step towards the integration of T/R module front-ends.
the GaN technology is a very attractive technology for the development of high-power, robust, low-noise ampliﬁers and switches for T/R module frontends.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are developing a set of robust, high-power MMICs on GaN for T/R module front-ends.

we have developed a GaN MMIC process, which enables the fabrication of robust GaN T/R switches and LNA's, all based on a single GaN technology, and which are able to withstand high CW input power levels.
we developed a robust GaN MMiC chipset for T/R module front end integration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a single process for the design of all the T/R front-end components will lead to the development of highly-integrated T/R modules, with reduced cost and size.
the GaN MMICs are robust enough to be used in fully integrated T/R modules.
the use of a single process for the design of the T/R module front end can be very beneficial for cost and time-to-market reasons.
